problems.h4: AdBlue System & DPF Clogging - Why the Ford Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue (TZDA/BNBU/QXWA/TXWA) Suffers Premature Blockages
problems.affectedModels: Ford Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue (TZDA, BNBU, QXWA, TXWA, 2020-present)
problems.rootCause: Frequent short, low-speed urban journeys prevent the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) from reaching the high temperatures required for active regeneration. Combined with AdBlue crystallisation, this increases exhaust backpressure and can trigger engine limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical clean of DPF, AdBlue system flush, and ECU reset
repairOptions.longevity: Temporary fix; blockage will return if driving habits do not change

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if DPF failure has caused secondary turbo or EGR damage

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Leaks - Why the Ford Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue (TZDA/BNBU/QXWA/TXWA) Loses Coolant
problems.affectedModels: Ford Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue (TZDA, BNBU, QXWA, TXWA, 2020-present)
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler internal matrix can develop micro-fractures over time, allowing coolant to mix with exhaust gases. This leads to unexplained coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and potential hydrolock or head gasket failure if ignored.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early and no internal engine damage has occurred

repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if coolant ingestion has caused piston or cylinder head damage

items.question: What are the signs of AdBlue or DPF failure in a Ford Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue?
items.answer: AdBlue or DPF failure in the Ford Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue usually presents as a persistent engine management light, reduced power (limp mode), and poor fuel economy.
keyPoints: You may notice a warning message on the dashboard indicating "AdBlue System Fault" or "DPF Full".
The vehicle may refuse to regenerate, leading to increased exhaust backpressure.
Ignoring these signs can lead to secondary turbocharger or EGR damage.

items.question: What is the difference between the TZDA and TXWA Ford Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue engines?
items.answer: The primary difference between the TZDA and TXWA codes fitted to the Ford Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue is the power output and associated drivetrain configuration.
keyPoints: The TZDA produces 150 PS and is available in both FWD and AWD configurations across Zetec, Titanium, and ST-Line trims.
The TXWA produces 190 PS and is exclusively paired with AWD, typically found in higher-spec ST-Line and Vignale trims.
Mechanically, they share the same core EcoBlue block, but the TXWA features a larger turbocharger and different ECU mapping.
